point: How does a user who installed overnight with `claude plugin install overnight@ccpm` get the `overnight` command in their terminal, given that Claude Code puts a plugin's files under ~/.claude/plugins/cache/ccpm/overnight/<version>/ and onto no PATH, and that no plugin in ccpm or claude-plugins-official ships a terminal command to follow? Options: (a) after the install, the user runs one link command, once, that puts `overnight` in ~/.local/bin, pointing at the marketplace's copy at ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ccpm/plugins/overnight/, which `claude plugin marketplace update` keeps current; (b) a skill, `/overnight:start`, starts the work from inside Claude Code as a process apart from the session, so the user never opens a terminal, though the agreed solution says the user starts it from a terminal; (c) the user types the full path with `python3` each time. I recommend (a), as it keeps the agreed start from a terminal, costs the user one command at install, and survives plugin updates without a new link.
